blocked_candidates.reason: Birth in Finland to foreign parents is not sufficient merely because no citizenship has actually been acquired. Entitlement to another nationality and statutory exceptions must also be assessed; do not teach the blanket source rule.
A negative decision alone does not establish immediate unlawful residence. Service, enforceability, appeal and other grounds matter.

Emergency social assistance responsibility must distinguish wellbeing services counties from municipal housing and voluntary providers. The source list is not a reliable nationwide allocation of current responsibility.
Migri states that the ministries prepare the allocation and the Government decides. The source incorrectly attributes the final allocation decision to the ministries.
Three years is normally a deadline for the first integration plan, not an absolute eligibility ceiling for every integration service. Exceptions and extensions exist.
A home municipality affects service access but is not an absolute prerequisite for all public services, including urgent care and other statutory routes.
A no-show interpreting charge is service- and legal-basis-specific. No current nationwide charging rule established for this unrestricted statement.
Temporary protection is not a fixed numerical refugee quota. The source wording about a limited number risks conflating two different systems.
Current Migri guidance includes additional eligibility qualifications dated August 2026. The source nationality/return condition alone is incomplete; current guidance must be consulted.

Current and extension guidance contain different treatment of third-country permanent residents of Ukraine. The source conflates distinct eligibility groups; no unqualified eligibility card published.
Family eligibility refers back to incompletely defined groups and omits current nationality restrictions. The date alone cannot establish eligibility.
Permanent EU residence is a right acquired when conditions are met; an optional certificate is not what creates the right. Source conflates the right with its documentation.
Blanket family-based permit requirement omits EU and Nordic routes and existing residence rights. Qualified family membership and route-selection cards cover sound adjacent claims.
Work starting only after this permit is granted is not universally true where another valid right to work already exists.
An A permit does not itself automatically register a home municipality. DVV assesses and registers the applicable conditions.
The continued existence of the old ground is not sufficient by itself: the current permit and general requirements still apply.
A refusal alone cannot be turned into an unconditional immediate departure instruction. Applicable removal decision, time limits, enforceability and other rights must be checked.
A refusal or rejected appeal alone is an incomplete departure rule. Further appeal, enforceability and any separate lawful ground matter.
The general rule concerns intended residence of at least a year, not universally having already completed a year. Some temporary-protection situations differ.
Home municipality does not equalise every right and obligation with every permanent resident. Citizenship, immigration status and individual benefit criteria still matter.
OPH is not the competent authority for every foreign qualification; employers, institutions and profession-specific regulators may decide.
The blanket YKI fee statement omits current exemptions, including qualifying advanced-level Finnish/Swedish tests from 2026.

Border procedure is a procedural setting with statutory conditions, not simply a synonym for accelerated processing or rejection without examination. Current EU Pact and national implementation require distinctions.

verification_sources.findings: First plan normally within three years; first plan at most one year; overall normal duration two years with statutory exceptions and extensions. Do not equate the first-plan deadline with all service eligibility.
Municipal integration responsibility and 2025 reform; individual assessment and services.
Integration Act framework; individual plans and municipal responsibilities. Cards do not assert universal entitlement.
Benefit conditions include registered jobseeking and participation in agreed integration/employment measures.
Employer or institution assesses many qualifications; regulated professions and specified posts require OPH or another competent authority.
Some advanced Finnish/Swedish YKI examinations are exempt from fees from 2026; blanket fee claim blocked.
Appropriate YKI results can demonstrate citizenship language proficiency; not a substitute for other citizenship requirements.
Home municipality requires statutory conditions and registration; a personal identity code alone is insufficient.
Personal data and home municipality registration are distinct matters.
Nordic citizens staying over six months notify DVV; EU registration follows a separate route.
EU/Swiss/Liechtenstein residence registration at Migri for stays over three months; Nordics register with DVV.
Permanent EU right after five years lawful continuous residence. Distinguish right from certificate.
Permanent permit rules changed January 2026. No old duration-only eligibility question created; cards require current conditions and distinguish P from A/B.
Sufficient resources and general permit conditions; family of Finnish citizen exception. Permit, identity and work rights are not interchangeable.
Finnish spouse route; current general and age conditions apply. Question isolates the income requirement rather than promising a permit.
Continuation of work during timely extension has conditions; a pending application is not unrestricted work authorisation.
Extension after domestic violence is individually assessed; evidence, general conditions and circumstances matter.
Special extension or certificate for exploited workers with an existing work-entitling permit; certificate can expand work rights.
Trafficking can support a residence permit subject to statutory assessment; not automatic.
Statutory border procedure imposes designated-area residence restrictions; not a generic definition of all accelerated asylum procedures.
EU Pact changes from June 2026; temporary-protection work rights remain unchanged. Avoid obsolete procedural absolutes.
Earlier-application guidance confirms legal counsel and legal-aid office/reception-centre route; no old deadline or fee rule imported into cards.
Asylum applicants do not ordinarily receive Kela benefits before a residence permit. Cards distinguish reception support and avoid saying no social protection exists.
Parliament decides annual quota; ministries prepare, Government decides allocation; UNHCR proposes people, Finland selects; emergency cases may be selected without interview.

Eligibility is qualified and time-sensitive. August 2026 wording and different listed groups make the source blanket eligibility rules unsuitable. Application is registered by police/border authority.
Extension and third-country-group guidance must be distinguished from new-application eligibility; no unqualified third-country eligibility claim taught.
Work can begin upon registered application for temporary protection; checked alongside current Migri Pact guidance that rights remain unchanged.
Removal enforceability and appeal vary; follow the individual decision and any court suspension, not an automatic immediate-departure rule.
Assisted voluntary return has eligibility conditions; can include practical help and financial/service assistance.
STM December 2025 announcement: urgent and individually necessary nonurgent care; question preserves individual medical assessment and does not promise every planned treatment.
Citizenship through parents depends on birth location, marriage and established parentage. Foreign birth with unmarried Finnish father uses declaration.
Citizenship through Finnish birth mother or Finnish father married to mother; not unconditional birthright citizenship.
Declaration groups include former citizens, Nordic citizens, qualifying young adults 18–22 and adoptees 12–17.
Nordic declaration requires five recent years, qualifying mode of Nordic citizenship and other conditions; card tests duration only with explicit other-conditions caveat.
Multiple nationality allowed; possible loss at 22 without sufficient connection, fraud, or annulled parentage under conditions. No automatic universal loss asserted.

other_source_issues: Original Swedish anthology preserved. Blocking retains CORE scores and does not recalibrate priority.
A/B are both fixed-term; the source sometimes calls both temporary. Cards use tidsbegränsat and reserve tillfälligt for B.
B-permit home-municipality card tests possibility under conditions, not each incidental route listed in its supporting sentences.
Citizenship requirements and permit rules are qualified; no future citizenship-test requirement or obsolete numerical threshold introduced.
Reuse links consolidate equivalent earlier learning points. Multiple source sentences may support a single focused card without every example becoming a separate question.
Temporary-protection pages contain differing eligibility/validity formulations. Uncertain group eligibility is blocked instead of treating an old extension rule as a universal current exclusion.
YKI fee and qualification-recognition absolutes are blocked even though adjacent valid institutional learning points have cards.
coverage_note: Source IDs include context and consolidation links. Coverage concerns selected learning points, not every detail in every linked sentence. Source itself was preserved. CORE priorities were not reduced for obsolete claims.
